Off Book: Give Me My Line
She gets one night on stage. He keeps teaching her his ex's pauses.
An understudy gets one night in the lead, opposite a star who still plays the breakup the way his ex did. She wants her own line — and nothing on stage she didn't agree to.

Mara Quinn has covered the lead in The Last Ferry for eight months, and Friday the original star — Theo Ward's ex, Delia — is out. Theo isn't the director and has no say over Mara, but he keeps demonstrating the pause, the kiss, the tears exactly as Delia played them, off a recording he labeled 'good one.' Mara wants to play Hazel her own way: laughing first at the breakup, a distance where the kiss used to be. You decide how much she risks, what she agrees to, and whether the man who finally listens gets dinner or just a curtain call.
The stage manager who calls every cue from the booth — and hears everything on headset.
If nobody speaks up, Mara spends her one night as someone else's ghost, and Theo never learns the play can survive a new reading.
